summary: Crow Reservation tower registered in 2022, dated 1930s with no construction year in the sources; a 1957 survey describes it as a 70-foot wooden tower.

facts.agency: Crow Agency - Bureau of Indian Affairs

events.note: Lightning-set fire in the Wolf Mountains, dated July 19, 1956; sighted from the lookout station and controlled after about four hours (Billings Gazette, as reprinted).
Survey description records the tower as a four-legged wooden structure, 70 feet in height.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: The tower is about 10 miles east of Lodge Grass.
The tower is on the Crow Indian Reservation.
The register dates the tower to the 1930s.
A 1957 survey description says the tower was a four-legged wooden structure about 70 feet tall.
evidence.quote: THE TOWER IS SUPPORTED BY A FOUR LEGGED WOODEN STRUCTURE AND IS 70 FEET IN HEIGHT
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1957

evidence.supports: A lightning-set fire in the Wolf Mountains was controlled after about four hours.
evidence.quote: A lightning-set fire in the Wolf Mountains was controlled after fire fighters battled the blaze for four hours.

evidence.supports: The fire was sighted from the lookout station and reported to the station at Crow Agency.
evidence.quote: The fire first was sighted from the Wolf Mountain lookout station on top of the Wold Mountains and reported to the station in Crow Agency.

evidence.supports: All firefighting equipment at Crow Agency was already fighting two other fires, so the information went to the Miller ranch.
evidence.quote: However, all fire fighting equipment in Crow Agency was battling two other fires on the reservation so the information was relayed to the Miller ranch.

evidence.supports: The tower is in Big Horn County, Montana.
The register recorded the tower on April 12, 2022.
The register names the Crow Agency office of the Bureau of Indian Affairs as administrator.
evidence.quote: Crow Agency - Bureau of Indian Affairs

evidence.supports: The register's description section has no details yet.
The register places the tower on the Crow Tribe's land in Big Horn County.

corrections.why: No source read states a permission rule for the tower. The register names the Crow Agency BIA office as administrator, and firelookout.com places the tower on the Crow Indian Reservation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 5,152 ft (1,570 m) and firelookout.com gives 5217 ft. The record uses the register figure. The gap is about 65 ft and is not used in the story.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: no construction year beyond the register's 1930s, no staffing history, no dated current-condition source, and no source for the record's permission access level. Height 70 ft converted to 21.3 m, taken from a 1957 survey description, so it may be out of date. The register's status is standing per the record; no dated source read confirms current condition. A 1992 Billings Gazette item on the site was left out because it concerns private individuals and is not needed for the lookout's history. Search budget overran: three WebSearch/websearch.py queries were run against this tower, not two. A groups.io discussion returned no text when fetched, so it is not used.
